skill.name: gitops-workflow
skill.description: Guide AI coding agents through GitOps workflows for Kubernetes using ArgoCD, Flux, declarative manifests, sync policies, progressive delivery, and secret management.
skill.summary: Set up GitOps workflows for Kubernetes with ArgoCD, Flux, sync policies, and deployment patterns.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown documentation examples for GitOps commands, YAML manifests, or expected public URLs. The main confirmed risk is the Flux install command that pipes network-fetched shell code into sudo, with additional operational risk from cluster-changing kubectl, argocd, flux, and kubeseal examples.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into sudo bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-sudo pattern with package-manager installation, checksum verification, or a pinned downloadable binary workflow.

remediation.issue: Cluster-changing commands are shown without safety gates.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to review context, namespace, target cluster, and production impact before running kubectl, flux, or argocd sync commands.

remediation.issue: Secret-handling examples rely on local secret files.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit cleanup and storage guidance for unsealed secret files, and prefer external secret managers for production workflows.

content.value_statement: Kubernetes delivery is hard to keep consistent across teams and clusters. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design GitOps workflows with ArgoCD, Flux, sync policies, and safe deployment patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains OpenGitOps principles for declarative, versioned, pulled, and reconciled systems.
Shows ArgoCD installation, application manifests, and app-of-apps repository structure.
Shows Flux bootstrap, GitRepository resources, and Kustomization resources.
Provides sync policy examples for automated prune, self-heal, retry, wait, and timeout behavior.
Documents progressive delivery examples with canary and blue-green rollout settings.
Covers GitOps secret approaches using External Secrets Operator and Sealed Secrets.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a complete production platform design.
It does not validate live cluster permissions, network access, or repository credentials.
Some commands can change Kubernetes clusters if copied and run directly.
Security controls such as SSO, RBAC, and secret management still need environment-specific review.

use_cases.title: Plan a New GitOps Rollout
use_cases.description: Create a repository layout and deployment flow for a Kubernetes application managed from Git.

use_cases.title: Standardize ArgoCD or Flux Setup
use_cases.description: Compare setup steps and resource definitions before adopting ArgoCD or Flux for continuous delivery.

use_cases.title: Improve Deployment Safety
use_cases.description: Add sync policies, progressive delivery, approval gates, and secret management patterns to existing workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Explain GitOps Basics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a first GitOps workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gitops-workflow skill to explain the main GitOps principles for my Kubernetes team. Include how Git, ArgoCD, and Flux fit together.

prompt_templates.title: Design Repository Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Team needs a practical layout for applications and infrastructure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gitops-workflow skill to propose a GitOps repository structure for staging and production. Include app folders, infrastructure folders, and ArgoCD application placement.

prompt_templates.title: Compare ArgoCD and Flux
prompt_templates.scenario: Platform team is choosing a GitOps controller.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gitops-workflow skill to compare ArgoCD and Flux for our Kubernetes deployment workflow. Focus on setup, sync behavior, secret handling, and operational risks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gitops-workflow skill to review our production GitOps design. Check sync policies, pruning behavior, rollback flow, progressive delivery, RBAC, SSO, and secret management.

output_examples.input: Help me set up ArgoCD for a production namespace.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step plan covering namespace creation, ArgoCD installation, repository layout, application manifest fields, automated sync settings, and safety checks before production use.

output_examples.input: We need Flux to deploy one app from GitHub.
output_examples.output: A Flux workflow that covers bootstrap planning, GitRepository configuration, Kustomization settings, reconciliation intervals, and review points for credentials and branch selection.

output_examples.input: Our GitOps sync keeps failing after manual changes.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist for sync status, diffs, prune behavior, self-heal settings, forced sync risks, and alerts for recurring drift.

best_practices: Review cluster context, namespace, and repository target before running any generated command.
Use staging, approval gates, and progressive delivery before enabling automated production sync.
Keep plaintext secrets out of Git and document the approved secret management path.
anti_patterns: Do not run remote installer pipelines with elevated privileges without verification.
Do not enable automated prune in production before teams understand deletion impact.
Do not store Kubernetes secrets or long-lived repository tokens directly in Git.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan and document GitOps workflows for Kubernetes using ArgoCD, Flux, declarative manifests, and sync policies.

faq.question: Can it choose between ArgoCD and Flux?
faq.answer: It can compare setup and operating patterns, but the final choice should include your team model and compliance needs.

faq.question: Does it run Kubernetes commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides examples and guidance. Users should review commands before running them against any cluster.

faq.question: Does it cover production security?
faq.answer: It includes SSO, RBAC, audit logging, and secret management topics, but production controls need local review.

faq.question: Can it help with progressive delivery?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes canary and blue-green rollout examples and guidance for safer deployment promotion.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
